sanskrit_iast: brahmavādino vadanti purā vā auddālakir āruṇir uvāca brahmaṇe tvā prāṇāya juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi brahmaṇe tvāpānāya juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi brahmaṇe tvā vyānāya juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi brahmaṇe tvā samānāya juṣṭaṃ nirvapāmi kā etā devatā yāsām evaitaj juṣṭaṃ nirvapaty ṛco vai brahmaṇaḥ prāṇa ṛcām evaitaj juṣṭaṃ nirvapati yajūṃṣi vai brahmaṇo 'pāno yajuṣām evaitaj juṣṭam nirvapati sāmāni vai brahmaṇo vyānaḥ sāmnām evaitaj juṣṭaṃ nirvapaty atharvāṇo vai brahmaṇaḥ samāno 'tharvaṇām evaitaj juṣṭaṃ nirvapati |
meaning: ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति पुरा वा औद्दालकिर् आरुणिर् उवाच ब्रह्मणे त्वा प्राणाय जुष्टं निर्वपामि ब्रह्मणे त्वापानाय जुष्टं निर्वपामि ब्रह्मणे त्वा व्यानाय जुष्टं निर्वपामि ब्रह्मणे त्वा समानाय जुष्टं निर्वपामि का एता देवता यासाम् एवैतज् जुष्टं निर्वपत्य् ऋचो वै ब्रह्मणः प्राण ऋचाम् एवैतज् जुष्टं निर्वपति यजूंषि वै ब्रह्मणो ऽपानो यजुषाम् एवैतज् जुष्टम् निर्वपति सामानि वै ब्रह्मणो व्यानः साम्नाम् एवैतज् जुष्टं निर्वपत्य् अथर्वाणो वै ब्रह्मणः समानो ऽथर्वणाम् एवैतज् जुष्टं निर्वपति ।
text_mt: The theologians say: Formerly, indeed, Auddālaki Āruṇi said, “I measure you out agreeable to the Brahman, to the in-breath; I measure you out agreeable to the Brahman, to the out-breath; I measure you out agreeable to the Brahman, to the diffused breath; I measure you out agreeable to the Brahman, to the equalising breath.” Which are these deities for whom he thus measures [it] out as agreeable? The verses are the in-breath of the Brahman; it is agreeable to the verses that he thus measures it out. The sacrificial formulas are the out-breath of the Brahman; it is agreeable to the sacrificial formulas that he thus measures it out. The sāman melodies are the diffused breath of the Brahman; it is agreeable to the sāman melodies that he thus measures it out. The Atharvans are the equalising breath of the Brahman; it is agreeable to the Atharvans that he thus measures it out. It is a four-platter offering; for four are these Vedas, and he makes them share in it. The Veda is the root of the Brahman; it is the root of the Vedas that the officiating priests eat. That is the nature of boiled rice for the priests as boiled rice for the priests.

sanskrit_iast: catuḥśarāvo bhavati catvāro hīme vedās tān eva bhāginaḥ karoti mūlaṃ vai brahmaṇo vedo vedānām evaitan mūlaṃ yad ṛtvijaḥ prāśnanti tad brahmaudanasya brahmaudanatvam |
meaning: चतुःशरावो भवति चत्वारो हीमे वेदास् तान् एव भागिनः करोति मूलं वै ब्रह्मणो वेदो वेदानाम् एवैतन् मूलं यद् ऋत्विजः प्राश्नन्ति तद् ब्रह्मौदनस्य ब्रह्मौदनत्वम् ।

sanskrit_iast: niśi carman brahmā brahmaudanaṃ nirvapati rakṣāṃsi vai devānāṃ yajñam ājighāṃsaṃs tāni brahmaṇāpāghnata brahma brahmā brahmaṇaiva yajñād rakṣāṃsy apahanti |
meaning: निशि चर्मन् ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मौदनं निर्वपति रक्षांसि वै देवानां यज्ञम् आजिघांसंस् तानि ब्रह्मणापाघ्नत ब्रह्म ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मणैव यज्ञाद् रक्षांस्य् अपहन्ति ।
text_mt: At night, on a hide, the Brahman priest measures out the boiled rice for the priests. The demons wished to destroy the sacrifice of the gods; they struck them down with the Brahman. The Brahman priest is the Brahman; with the Brahman itself he strikes the demons away from the sacrifice. It is a four-platter offering; four are the quarters: with the quarters itself he strikes the demons away from the sacrifice. It consists of unbroken grains of rice for prosperity. Unpurified, unfit for sacrifice, unworthy of the sacrifice, having spoken untruth is he who establishes the sacred fires without having paid off his debts. Having made him take hold [of the oblation] from behind, he offers these oblations with clarified butter, [saying], “Whatever offence to the gods, whatever [debt] I, not gambling, incurred...” He purifies him; purified, fit for sacrifice, worthy of the sacrifice, he establishes the sacred fires. He offers these twenty-one oblations. That sun is the twenty-first; he is Savitṛ. That is the strainer of the god Savitṛ; with that strainer of Savitṛ he purifies him. With “Whatever [sin occurred] in the intermediate region...”, the fires release him from this sin. With “The breaker, the crusher...”, the fires drive away consumption from him, [and] sorcery and Nirṛti. With “Together with lustre...”, he invokes a blessing.

text_mt: The gods and the Asuras waited upon the establishment of the sacred fires, performing equally: whatever the gods did, that the Asuras did. Those gods, having set down this boiled rice, offered these oblations with clarified butter. The Asuras did not follow after [them]. Thereupon the gods prospered, the Asuras were defeated. He who, knowing thus, having set down this boiled rice, offers these oblations with clarified butter, does so so that his rival may not follow after; he prospers by himself, his rival is defeated. Having said, “To the wise creator...”, he offers of the boiled rice; he appeases the anger of the gods. He offers these oblations with clarified butter for one about to undertake the four-monthly sacrifices, for one about to undergo consecration; he purifies him. Purified, fit for sacrifice, worthy of the sacrifice, he sacrifices; purified, fit for sacrifice, worthy of the sacrifice, he undergoes consecration. [Those] about to establish [the fires] on the morrow stay awake the night. Sleep is blind darkness; he frees him from blind darkness. They sing with ritual artifices, for with ritual artifices they accomplish everything.

sanskrit_iast: śva ādhāsyamāna rātrīṃ jāgrati tamo vā andhaṃ svapnas tamasa evainam andhaso muñcati śilpair gāyanti śilpair hi sarvaṃ kurvanti |

sanskrit_iast: dhārayaty etam agniṃ na māṃsam aśnīyān na striyam upeyād adhaḥ śayīta na vipravasen nāsya gṛhād agniṃ hareyur nāhareyur anyata ātmano gopīthāyā 'gnim etam ādhāya samidādhānāntaṃ kuryād varaṃ dadānīti vācaṃ visṛjate 'śānto vā eṣa bhūtvā yajamānam abhyaiti vareṇa caivainaṃ satyayā ca vācā śamayati |

text_mt: He maintains this fire. He should not eat meat, he should not approach a woman, he should lie on the ground, he should not go on a journey, they should not carry fire away from his house, nor should they bring [it] from elsewhere, for the protection of himself. Having established this fire, he should make it end with the placing of kindling sticks. He releases speech, saying, “May I give a wish!” This [fire], having become unappeased, approaches the sacrificer; with a wish and with true speech he appeases it.

sanskrit_iast: rathantaruṃ gārhapatya ādhīyamāne gāyaty ayaṃ vai loko rathantaram ayaṃ gārhapatyo 'smiṃs tena loke pratitiṣṭhaty agniṃ jyotir avarunddhe vāmadevyaṃ dakṣiṇāgnā ādhīyamāne gāyaty antarikṣaṃ vai vāmadevyam antarikṣaṃ dakṣiṇāgnir antarikṣe tena pratitiṣṭhati vāyuṃ jyotir avarunddhe bṛhad āhavanīya ādhīyamāne gāyaty asau vai loko bṛhad asā āhavanīyo 'muṣmiṃs tena loke pratitiṣṭhati sūryaṃ jyotir avarunddhe |
meaning: रथन्तरुं गार्हपत्य आधीयमाने गायत्य् अयं वै लोको रथन्तरम् अयं गार्हपत्यो ऽस्मिंस् तेन लोके प्रतितिष्ठत्य् अग्निं ज्योतिर् अवरुन्द्धे वामदेव्यं दक्षिणाग्ना आधीयमाने गायत्य् अन्तरिक्षं वै वामदेव्यम् अन्तरिक्षं दक्षिणाग्निर् अन्तरिक्षे तेन प्रतितिष्ठति वायुं ज्योतिर् अवरुन्द्धे बृहद् आहवनीय आधीयमाने गायत्य् असौ वै लोको बृहद् असा आहवनीयो ऽमुष्मिंस् तेन लोके प्रतितिष्ठति सूर्यं ज्योतिर् अवरुन्द्धे ।
text_mt:
He sings the Rathantara chant while the Gārhapatya is being established. This world is the Rathantara chant, this

Gārhapatya fire is this [world]; thereby he is established in this world; he secures Agni, the light. He sings the Vāmadevya chant while the Dakṣiṇāgni fire

is being established. The intermediate region is the Vāmadevya chant; the Dakṣiṇāgni fire is the intermediate region; thereby in the intermediate region

he is established; he secures Vāyu, the light. He sings the Bṛhat chant while the Āhavanīya fire is being established. That

world is the Bṛhat chant, that Āhavanīya fire is that [world]; thereby he is established in that world; he secures Sūrya, the light.

text_mt:
Regarding this they say: Sucked dry indeed are his fires, for whom, while they are being established, sāman melodies are sung. For calves

are the sāman melodies of the fires; they do not milk all desires for him; therefore sāman melodies should not be sung, so that the fires may not be milked out. These are the dear bodies of Soma, namely the sāman melodies; if they were sung elsewhere, they would deprive Soma

of his dear bodies, [and] Soma would not bend toward him. Therefore sāman melodies should not be sung,

text_mt:
This Gārhapatya is the house of the fires. This alone was [there], not the Āhavanīya, nor the Dakṣiṇāgni fire. Those

gods along with their wives cooked food in the Gārhapatya. Having cooked [it], they ate together; the wives of the gods did not eat going along [with them]. Those gods knew: “We are causing injury to the sacrifice. Let us

divide the fire!” They divided the fire. What was the third part of that fire, that the gods brought eastward on the morrow. It

It became the Āhavanīya fire for the gods: that is the reason why the Āhavanīya fire is called Āhavanīya. Therefore day after day it is led forward eastward. The third portion of that fire the divine ancestors enclosed; they led it toward the south. It

became the Dakṣiṇāgni fire: that is the reason why the Dakṣiṇāgni fire is called Dakṣiṇāgni. Just as a little son born of a Śūdra womb eats everything, both what is fit for sacrifice and what is unfit for sacrifice, even so the fire from the roaster eats everything, both what is fit for sacrifice and what is unfit for sacrifice. Belonging to the Asuras, indeed, is that

fire from the roaster. When one makes an oblation in it, his oblations become belonging to the Asuras. He cooks before[hand] what is cooked for the Asuras,

not for the ancestors. Now, if someone desires, "Let my share for the ancestors be raw and cooked," having led forward fire from the Gārhapatya fire, he should offer oblations: his share for the ancestors indeed becomes raw and cooked. The third portion of it the wives of the gods enclosed: it became the Gārhapatya fire; that is the reason why the Gārhapatya fire is called Gārhapatya. Therefore, with the Gārhapatya fire enclosed, they make the wives participate in the sacrifice. The offerings are of clarified butter; clarified butter is semen; from semen offspring are born: [it is] for procreation. One should make the mark of the Gārhapatya fire round, for this world is round, commensurate with this world; [one should make that] of the Dakṣiṇāgni fire a half-moon, for the intermediate region is a half-moon, commensurate with the intermediate region; the heavenly world is four-cornered, therefore the Āhavanīya fire is four-cornered, to attain the heavenly world.

text_mt: The theologians say: "These are indeed the dwellings of the gods, namely the Gārhapatya fire, the Dakṣiṇāgni fire, and the Āhavanīya fire." One should make the mark of the Gārhapatya fire round, for this world is round; it is twenty-eight finger-breadths, commensurate with the Śakvarī [metre]; the Śakvarī has seven feet; animals are Śākvara: he secures animals. [One should make that] of the Dakṣiṇāgni fire a half-moon, for the intermediate region is a half-moon, commensurate with the intermediate region; that which is the moon is indeed the food of the deities: he feeds the deities with food; it is thirty-two finger-breadths, commensurate with the Anuṣṭubh [metre]; with the Anuṣṭubh he makes vigour; with the Anuṣṭubh he furnishes the sacrificer with vigour. One should make that of the Āhavanīya fire four-cornered, for that world is four-cornered; it is of the measure of a cubit, for the self is of this measure, commensurate with Prajāpati; Prajāpati is food: he furnishes him with edible food. Having offered, he should let the fires rest; he is born with offspring and cattle. Now they say: "Let loose, the bull grows." With [the verse], "With the measure of heaven spread wide with width," he spreads it out. Just as [a fire] blazing up adds further, even so he deposits that fiery energy in it successively. Regarding that, they say: "Who ought to awaken an eminent one who is fast asleep?" Therefore he should not let [them] rest. He who thus knows their dwelling becomes possessed of a dwelling. For him who knows thus, [or] when one who knows thus spreads the fires, he becomes more prosperous.

text_mt: All the gods, having assembled, asked Prajāpati: "Whence will the triad of sacred fires come to be?" He, with his feet raised upward and his head on the earth below, performed austerity for a divine thousand years. From him tears fell away; in those very tears the horse was born. He rolled over, he shook himself, he made dung; he turned around and smelled [it]. From that dung a horse-part was born; and from the middle of the horse's flank it snorted; because it snorted from the middle of the horse's flank, the aśvattha tree was born. Its root is the Veda; the metres are the leaves; the branches are the recensions. Thus it is grown inside a śamī tree: that is the reason why grown inside a śamī tree is called grown inside a śamī tree.

text_mt: All the gods, having assembled, asked Prajāpati: "Does this fire arise from a pair, or from the fire-drill, or from the upper [drill]?" Prajāpati said to them: "Just as a man approaches a woman, and from that threefold pair, being churned, semen arises from the man—this upper fire-drill is the form of Viṣṇu, that is the form of the Gāyatrī—therefore from this pair fire is born when churned." The upper [drill] is twelve finger-breadths: twelve months are the year; [it is] for the attainment of the year. The cover is thirteen finger-breadths: these three worlds [and] ten months are the year; [it is] for the attainment of the year. The cord is three-pressed: these three worlds; in these very worlds he thrives.

text_mt: Agni fled from the gods; he ran away westward. Therefore the Adhvaryu churns the fire facing westward. In that he churns the fire facing westward, he summons that very Agni. When he sings a sāman melody to the smoke with [the verse], "Your brilliant smoke moves," he announces him to the gods. When he sings a sāman melody to the fire with [the verse], "The best finder of a path," he makes a proclamation for him to the gods. A child is this fire; possessed of fiery energy are the sāman melodies. Therefore at the establishment of the sacred fires sāman melodies are not sung; for he does not endure their fiery energy. The fires of one who has established the sacred fires weep if sāman melodies are sung for him prior to the Soma [sacrifice]. Therefore they are to be sung at the Soma [sacrifice], not prior to the Soma [sacrifice], for the firehood of the fires, and also that they may possess fiery energy.

text_mt: The fire-drill is twenty-four finger-breadths: the Gāyatrī has twenty-four syllables, commensurate with the Gāyatrī; it is six finger-breadths wide: there are six seasons, he is established in the seasons. Viṣṇu is the spoke; this fire-drill is his wife: that is the reason why the fire-drill is called fire-drill. Its four finger-breadths that are at the tip are the head; the other four finger-breadths are the neck; the other four finger-breadths are the chest, the breast, the two arms, the two sides, the back, and the belly; the other four finger-breadths are the hips; the other four finger-breadths are the two thighs [and] the two knees; the other four finger-breadths are the two shanks [and] the feet. Thus the fire-drill is complete with all its limbs. If he churns in the head, the sacrificer dies of a head-disease. If in the mouth, he becomes speech-impaired. If in the neck, he stammers. If in the shoulders, he becomes paralysed on one side. If in the belly, the sacrificer dies of hunger. If in the two thighs, that belongs to the sorcerers; if in the shanks, to the Piśācas; if in the feet, to the flesh-eating [demons]. If he churns in the hips, that belongs to all the gods; through that the sacrificer goes to heaven, who knows thus. At the first churning [these] rules of place [apply], not in subsequent ones; and he arrives at falsehood who knows thus.

text_mt:
Thus ends the Brāhmaṇa on the establishment of the sacred fires.

The gods and the Asuras churned the essence of the waters. From it being churned, the nectar of immortality arose. The essence that flowed together from all sides was Soma; that is the somaness of Soma. Soma, indeed, is the moon. The gods consume it part by part. A person has sixteen parts: ‘lo-ma’ (hair) is two syllables, ‘tvak’ (skin) is two, ‘a-sṛk’ (blood) is two, ‘māṃ-sam’ (flesh) is two, ‘snā-yu’ (sinew) is two, ‘as-thi’ (bone) is two, ‘me-daḥ’ (fat) is two, ‘maj-jā’ (marrow) is two. These amount to sixteen. That sixteen-part person belongs to Soma. The Vasus consumed five parts of it, having made the earth their vessel. They desired immortality; they won immortality. Then indeed they became immortal, sated, satisfied. The Rudras consumed five parts of it, having made the intermediate region their vessel. They desired immortality; they won immortality. Then indeed they became immortal, sated, satisfied. The Ādityas consumed five parts of it, having made heaven their vessel. They desired immortality; they won immortality. Then indeed they became immortal, sated, satisfied. One part remained. Prajāpati gave it to Sinīvālī. With it, he dwelled together here among beasts, trees, and plants. Because he dwelled together (amā avasat), that is the new-moon-ness (amāvasyātva) of the new moon (amāvasyā). With it, he saw in the morning; because he saw (dadarśa), that is the vision-ness (darśatva) of the new-moon day (darśa). The gods, having been invigorated by the sacrifice, invigorated him again. Being full, he dwelled near the full-moon day; that is the full-moon-ness of the full moon. Therefore they say: ‘He who offers the new- and full-moon sacrifices goes conquering worlds.’ He attains equality of power, union, and co-residence with Soma, who, knowing thus, sacrifices with the new- and full-moon sacrifices.

text_mt: ‘Four horns’: these are declared to be the Vedas. / ‘Three are his feet’: the three pressings. / ‘Two heads’: the opening and concluding rites. / ‘Seven are his hands’: the seven meters. / Therefore there are seven flames, seven kindling sticks, [and] these seven worlds / in which the breaths move, hidden in secret caves, seven placed in each. / ‘Bound in three ways’: bound in three ways by formulas, Brāhmaṇas, and ritual handbooks. / ‘The bull roars’: his roaring is according to the sequence of the pressings / through the verses, formulas, melodies, and Atharvan [formulas], since with verses they praise him, with formulas they sacrifice to him, with melodies / they laud him, with Atharvan [formulas] they mutter. / ‘The great god’: Mahādeva. / ‘Entered mortals’: of human beings. The further parts of it are for explanation: The four horns became the four-faced, the four Vedas, the four yugas, / [and] the four fires. / Mount Kailāsa itself is by name one. Then in one-horned, two-horned, ten-horned, twelve-horned, / twenty-horned, twenty-two-horned, thirty-horned, thirty-two-horned, hundred-horned, thousand-horned, ten-million-horned, infinite-horned, Meru-horned, crystal-horned, ancestor-horned, human-horned, the sages speak of the earlier and later [limits] of the twelve Ādityas. He attains a full lifespan, he attains everything—lifespan, he attains everything, who knows thus.

text_mt: The gods and the Asuras did indeed perform equally at the sacrifice. Whatever the gods did, that the Asuras did. / Those gods saw these planetary offerings; with them they made Indra sacrifice. Those Asuras did not follow after [them]. Thereupon the gods / flourished, the Asuras perished. He who, knowing thus, sacrifices these planetary offerings, serves to keep his rival from following after him; he himself flourishes, his rival perishes. One should offer a rice cake boiled in ghee to the Sun; fiery energy he thereby purchases. A Śaukra offering of boiled rice [to Venus]; sacred luster he thereby purchases. To Bṛhaspati a boiled rice offering of wild rice in milk; lordship of speech he thereby purchases. To Mercury a cake on [several] potsherds; intellect he thereby purchases. To Mars a cake on one potsherd; glory he thereby purchases. To Saturn a boiled rice offering mixed with sesame seeds in ghee; fragrance he thereby purchases. To the Moon a cake on fifteen potsherds; long life he thereby purchases. To Rāhu a boiled rice offering; fearlessness he thereby purchases. To Ketu a boiled rice offering; unhindered state he thereby purchases. He becomes all these very things who, / knowing thus, should sacrifice with this [offering]. He offers supplementary oblations with clarified butter for the attainment of his wishes. He should sacrifice with this / who should desire: ‘May I become endowed with fiery energy, radiant, a lord of speech, intelligent, glorious, fragrant, long-lived, fearless, unhindered.’ ‘A single wheel arose, shining’—there are eighteen offering and invitatory verses / for the sake of uniformity. ‘Agni is gold, Soma is gold’ are the two clarified-butter portions. ‘Enkindled, O Agni,’ [and] ‘These, O Agni’ are the two concluding verses. He sacrifices aloud. That indeed is the highest among voices, which is aloud; he becomes highest among his equals. / ‘The Sun is endowed with fiery energy’—he offers supplementary oblations for the attainment of everything, for the securing of everything, who, knowing thus, / should sacrifice with this [offering].

text_mt: He says: 'I have entered upon brahmacarya.' For the sacred knowledge is Brahman; through Brahman he entrusts himself. He asks him: 'Who art thou by name?' For Prajāpati is 'Who' (Ka) by name. Having thus made him belong to Prajāpati, he initiates him possessing kinship. He says: 'Bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ.' Thereby he gives him these three worlds for the eating of food. 'Bhūḥ' is this world; 'bhuvaḥ' is the intermediate region; 'svaḥ' is that world. Thereby he gives him these three Vedas for the eating of food. 'Bhūḥ' is the verses; 'bhuvaḥ' is the sacrificial formulas; 'svaḥ' is the sāmans. He studies one, two, three, or all of these Vedas—he whom he initiates knowing thus. He says to him: 'To Ka do I commit thee.' For Ka is Prajāpati; to Prajāpati indeed he commits him. The celibate student does not die, nor does his celibate student die—[he] whom he initiates knowing thus. He says to him: 'To the god Savitṛ do I commit thee.' For whatever Savitṛ impels for creatures, that they do. Whatever he would do by himself, let him not think, 'I am doing this.' Let him only think, 'Savitṛ has impelled me.' Whatever is good, that Savitṛ impels for him; Savitṛ impels no evil for him—whom he initiates knowing thus. He says to him: 'To Bṛhaspati do I commit thee.' For Bṛhaspati is sacred knowledge; to sacred knowledge indeed he commits him. The celibate student does not die, nor does his celibate student die—whom he initiates knowing thus. He says to him: 'Thou art a celibate student.' For sacred knowledge is the eating of food; he thus places the eating of food in him. And moreover, the eating of food is immortality; he thus places immortality in him. He says to him: 'Sip water.' For water reached everything here; thereby he says to him: 'Attain everything.' Water is the eating of food; he thus places the eating of food in him. And moreover, the eating of food is immortality; he thus places immortality in him. He says to him: 'Do work.' For work is manly strength; by manly strength food is eaten. Work is the eating of food; he thus places the eating of food in him. And moreover, the eating of food is immortality; he thus places immortality in him. He says to him: 'Do not sleep by day.' For sleep is death; therefore he wards him off from it. Sleep is indeed death; therefore of one who dies they say: 'He has slept a long sleep.' Day is the eating of food; he thus places the eating of food in him. And moreover, the eating of food is immortality; he thus places immortality in him. He says to him: 'Restrain speech.' For speech is the eating of food; he thus places the eating of food in him. And moreover, the eating of food is immortality; he thus places immortality in him. These five eatings of food the teacher establishes in the celibate student before the recitation of the Sāvitrī verse. That celibate student is born together with the Sāvitrī. Regarding this they say: 'It should be recited after a year; for seed sown is born in a year.' But then they say: 'It should be recited after twelve days; twelve months are a year; he generates him by means of a year, for the attainment of a year.' He should recite it to him in the morning after three nights: three days, three nights, three evenings, three dawns—they amount to twelve; twelve months are a year; he generates him by means of a year, for the attainment of a year. That Sāvitrī is the entrance to these worlds and to these Vedas. He should not recite it standing, nor sitting with his knees raised, nor walking. Having spread out broadly, having made a lap, sitting facing east, he recites it to him who is sitting facing west. Prajāpati faces east; the gods follow after him facing west. The teacher is the Prajāpati of the celibate student; he thus fits him out from his proper abode. Now some say: 'He recites it to him sitting on the south side.' [They say:] 'If he should recite it to him there, the embryo would come out crosswise and harm [him].' Therefore, sitting facing east, he recites it to him sitting facing west. The breath is facing east; he thus places breath in him. He should recite it three times: there are three breaths—in-breath, diffused breath, out-breath; these he places in him. He should recite it twice: for there are two—in-breath and out-breath; in-breath and out-breath he places in him. At the end he recites it once continuously: for the breath is one; he thus places breath in him.

text_mt:
These worlds belonged to the Asuras. The gods said: 'Whosoever shall conquer whichever world, that

shall belong to him.' The Vasus conquered this world, the Rudras the intermediate region, the Ādityas heaven. Those

Vasus, having conquered this world, flew on toward the intermediate region. They said to the Rudras: 'What we conquer, let that

be shared between us.' The Vasus and the Rudras, having conquered the intermediate region, flew on toward heaven. They said to the Ādityas:

'What we conquer, let that be shared between us.' The Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas, having conquered that world, overpowered the Asuras in these very worlds. Then the gods came to be; the Asuras were defeated. The Vasus are the fathers, the Rudras the grandfathers, the Ādityas the great-grandfathers. Therefore they say: 'The ancestors are gods; the gods are ancestors.' Whichever ancestors of the gods drink Soma, them they satisfy with vessels of water. Therefore, water is given three times to one, twice to one, once to one: that amounts to six; they receive just as they conquered. When they drink water at the end of the food, that is the seventh; what is mixed with sesame on roots facing both directions, that is the eighth; when there is sprinkling around the balls of rice with a bowl, that is the ninth; when they move the water-jar to the south, that is the tenth. Therefore the ancestral rite is called 'ten-watered'. That makes ten; the Virāj has ten syllables; the Virāj is food; he establishes himself firmly in the Virāj, in the eating of food.

text_mt: The ancestors followed after a son being born, [thinking:] 'May he perform the ancestral rite for us.' He said: 'When shall I perform the ancestral rite?' They said: 'One who desires that he should not have to give it again should give the ancestral rite under the shadow of an elephant.' For having become an elephant, Svarbhānu overpowered that sun with his shadow. The divine ancestors nourished him. That is the abode of the divine ancestors—the shadow of an elephant. Therefore, he who desires that it should be inexhaustible, boundless, and increasingly abundant should give the ancestral rite under the shadow of an elephant. It becomes inexhaustible, boundless, and increasingly abundant for him who, knowing thus, gives the ancestral rite under the shadow of an elephant, for the inexhaustibility of the ancestors.

text_mt: Two indeed are the paths: the path of the gods and the path of the ancestors. Through the Agnihotra, indeed, the gods went to the heavenly world; through the sacrifice to the ancestors, [they went] to the world of the ancestors. Therefore both are to be sacrificed to, the path of the gods and the path of the ancestors. Having attained the heavenly world by both, they say: in the other world they became established with a kindling stick, and they approached the brahmins with food. They said to them, 'Shall we make [it] in the fire? I will make [it] in the fire. Let me make [it] in the fire.' They replied, 'Make [it]! Make [it] for yourself! Let it be made!' If he should desire of someone, 'May he possess offspring,' he should say at his sacrifice, 'Make [it]!' If he should desire of someone, 'May he possess cattle,' he should say at his sacrifice, 'Make [it] for yourself!' If he should desire of someone, 'May he become wealthier,' he should say at his sacrifice, 'Let it be made!' This offering which is the making in the fire belongs to Agni and Soma. By this very offering belonging to Agni and Soma, the sacrificer becomes wealthier in this world.

text_mt: Mind, indeed, does he yoke who yokes intending to sacrifice, for by mind the sacrifice is extended; it becomes a sacrifice. Then he has faith. The ancestors indeed follow one who has faith. Having heard of prosperity, they perform the prosperity-śrāddha; thereby they are desired and pleased by him. Indra, indeed, desiring offspring, sacrificed with the sacrifice to the ancestors. The Asuras sought to destroy his sacrifice. The All-Gods struck them down. When they perform [the offering] to the All-Gods beforehand, it is to ward off the Asuras. It should be given on [ground] sloping to the east. [Ground] sloping to the east is indeed a thunderbolt. With the thunderbolt, indeed, he wards off the demons from the sacrifice. The darbha grass has points to the south and points to the north. With those having points to the south, indeed, his ancestors approach; with those having points to the north, the gods. Therefore, inverted darbha grass is given to the brahmins so that the ancestors may approach. In this way his ancestors approach, for the ancestors are concealed from that sun, and the ancestors are also concealed from the gods and from humans. He cuts the sacrificial grass near the root: thereby [it belongs] to the ancestors; what is without the root, thereby to the gods, for both are sacrificed to. For they are concealed from the sight of man; thus indeed they are concealed.

meaning: इयं दुरुक्तात् परिबाधमान इति दुरुक्ता वर्जयित्वा परिबाधन्ते वर्णं पवित्रं पुनती न आगाद् इत्य् अपो वै वर्णम् एव पवित्रम् अलं करोति प्राणापानाभ्यां बलम् आभजन्तीति प्राणेवैपानाभ्यां बलं दधाति सुखा देवी सुभगा मेखलेयम् इत्य् आशिषम् एवाशास्ते सौभाग्यं वै सुखा देवी दधाति सहस्रम् आवि प्रतिरन्त आयुः । इति मेखलाब्राह्मणम् ।
text_mt: 'Warding off bad speech, this one...': avoiding bad speech, they ward [it] off. 'Purifying our form, the strainer has come to us': the waters indeed adorn the form as a strainer. 'Bringing strength through in-breath and out-breath': he places strength into the in-breath and out-breath. 'This pleasant, auspicious goddess, the girdle': he expresses a benediction. The pleasant goddess indeed bestows auspiciousness, 'extending our life a thousandfold.'
